name: Furbolg
summary: Furbolgs are a hulking, reclusive race of bear-men native to northern Kalimdor who lived in harmony with nature and the night elves for millennia. In the wake of the Third War, demonic corruption and lingering fel magic have driven nearly every tribe into a frenzied madness. Today, former friends have become vicious territorial predators, with only a tiny handful of tribes clinging to their sanity.

sections.title: Ancient Kinship
sections.body: Furbolgs trace their ancestry back to the jalgar of ancient Kalimdor and have long revered the wild god Ursoc. During the War of the Ancients ten thousand years ago, tribal packs united under chieftain Unng Ak to fight alongside night elves and tauren against the first demonic invasion. Following the Great Sundering, they chose seclusion deep in the northern woodlands, maintaining peaceful ties with night elf druids and forest wardens while living in simple harmony with the wild.

sections.title: The Scourge of Madness
sections.body: The Third War shattered the furbolgs' tranquil existence. The passage of the Burning Legion through Kalimdor left lingering fel taint across the soil and canopy of Ashenvale and Felwood. Simple-minded and deeply attuned to the land, the bear-men absorbed this corruption directly. Their wizened shamans were overthrown or silenced by bloodthirsty firebrands who channeled fel moss, dark talismans, and corrupt alchemy, transforming peaceful gatherers into rabid raiders who now attack travelers and night elf settlements on sight.

sections.title: The Unbroken Line
sections.body: Across northern Kalimdor, nearly every major tribe has succumbed: the Gnarlpine across Teldrassil, the Blackwood of Darkshore, the Thistlefur and Foulweald in Ashenvale, and the Deadwood and Winterfall of the northern highlands. Yet a few hold the line. Deep within the fortified tunnels connecting Felwood, Winterspring, and Moonglade, the Timbermaw tribe fiercely guards its sanity. Wary and isolated, the Timbermaw defend their hold against their crazed northern kin, desperate to preserve what remains of their uncorrupted culture.

faq.q: Why are the furbolgs attacking everyone?
faq.answer: The aftermath of the Third War left lingering demonic corruption throughout Kalimdor's northern forests. Because furbolgs are deeply attuned to nature, this taint seeped into their minds, driving their tribes into paranoid, violent frenzy and replacing their peaceful elders with aggressive chieftains.

faq.q: Were furbolgs always enemies of the night elves?
faq.answer: No. For thousands of years, furbolgs and night elves were peaceful neighbors and close allies. They fought shoulder to shoulder against the Burning Legion during the War of the Ancients, and night elf druids maintained gentle relations with tribal settlements until the recent wave of madness took hold.

faq.q: Are there any furbolgs who are still friendly?
faq.answer: Yes. The Timbermaw tribe maintains an uncorrupted enclave inside Timbermaw Hold, the crossroads tunnel system between Felwood, Moonglade, and Winterspring. Though deeply suspicious of outsiders, they will tolerate travelers who prove their enmity toward the tainted Deadwood and Winterfall tribes.

faq.q: What is wrong with the furbolgs on Teldrassil?
faq.answer: The Gnarlpine tribe on Teldrassil has fallen under the sway of fel moss, an insidious corruption spreading through the world tree's boughs. Under Chieftain Ursal the Mauler, the corrupted Gnarlpine abandoned their traditional villages and overran sacred sites like the Ban'ethil Barrow Den and Starbreeze Village.

faq.q: Who is behind the corruption of the Winterfall in Winterspring?
faq.answer: The Winterfall are secretly manipulated by a satyr named Xandivious, who lurks within their chieftain's den. The tribe's frenzy is sustained by Winterfall Firewater, brewed from tainted materials inside Felwood's Deadwood Cauldron and ferried north through the mountain passes.

faq.q: Can corrupted furbolgs ever be cured?
faq.answer: Night elf sentinels and druids have attempted to cleanse individual tribes using moonwell waters and sacred relics, but broad recovery has proven nearly impossible. With satyrs and dark relics actively driving the corruption deeper, defenders often have no choice but to cull hostile packs to protect settlements.

angles.text: For night elves, the fall of the furbolgs is a heartbreaking tragedy. Tribes who were trusted woodland allies for ten thousand years have become feral predators threatening Astranaar and the sacred barrows of Teldrassil.
Druids mourn the bear-men as kindred spirits of Ursoc whose connection to nature has been weaponized by fel taint, making tribal unrest a direct symptom of the land's broader sickness.
The Horde views the hostile tribes of Ashenvale as territorial roadblocks, clearing aggressive packs like the Foulweald and Thistlefur to secure supply routes and outposts along the forest fringe.
